update.title: Built Power Manager to coordinate desktop power actions
update.summary: Connected shutdown, restart, and sleep requests to visual transitions through one command-line controller, with selectable effects and a preview mode.

preview.description: The desktop menu connected to Power Manager, with shutdown, sleep, restart, logout, and Windows restart controls.

blocks.body: I built Power Manager as the controller between a desktop power menu and Linux power actions. A menu or command can request shutdown, restart, or sleep; Power Manager starts the selected visual transition and coordinates the handoff to the operating system. The same controller also supports logout and hibernation.

blocks.description: The animated path moves from a menu or command-line request, through a transition that covers the display, to the selected system power action.

blocks.body:
## Time the action to the animation

Power Manager launches an effect through Shutdown Effect, the companion animation system. It listens for `READY`, meaning the overlay is visible, and `BLACK`, meaning the display is fully covered, to time the power-action handoff. The effect holds its covered frame while the action proceeds.

I kept effect selection separate from the power commands, so changing the animation does not require rewriting the shutdown or sleep workflow.

blocks.label: Shutdown Effect: the animation lifecycle and visual effects

blocks.body:
## Preview a transition without powering off

I added a test mode that plays the selected animation, holds the covered frame for a chosen duration, and then ends the effect without issuing a power action. It also requests desktop and cursor cleanup, so animations can be checked from the same controller used by the power menu.

An explicit `none` option skips the animation when an immediate action is preferred.

blocks.code:
# Preview the fade effect, then return to the desktop
power-manager test --animation fade --hold 3

# Restart with a fade transition
power-manager reboot --animation fade

# Suspend immediately, without an animation
power-manager suspend --animation none
blocks.description: The same command supports an animation preview, an animated restart, and sleep without a transition.
